concepts.name: capture_rate_vs_subject_speed
concepts.claim: Too low a rate loses motion and looks jerky; rate must scale with subject speed.
concepts.example: 4 mph walking -> minimum 64 fps; orthodox 16 fps allows only 1 mph
concepts.assumption: Linear relationship between subject speed and required frame rate; unverified by us.

concepts.name: slow_motion_playback_mechanism
concepts.claim: Shooting faster than playback rate slows subject on screen proportionally.
concepts.example: 2000 fps capture at 16 fps playback -> bullet moves at snail's pace
concepts.assumption: Constant playback rate; no dropped or duplicated frames during projection.

concepts.name: print_twice_method
concepts.claim: Each negative printed twice halves effective frame rate; 2x undetected, 3x looks disjointed.
concepts.assumption: Applies to film prints; digital frame duplication behavior is our inference, untested.

concepts.name: time_lapse_interval
concepts.claim: One turn one picture at stated intervals; interval too long spoils blending into sudden jerks.
concepts.assumption: Interval choice is empirical and subject-dependent; no formula given.

checkpoints.name: motion_step_check
checkpoints.instruction: Inspect consecutive frames: does fast motion advance in discrete jumps rather than smooth arcs? Maps to C1 jerkiness criterion.

checkpoints.name: playback_ratio_check
checkpoints.instruction: Compute ratio: capture_fps_equivalent / output_fps. No Talbot figure transfers directly; use as relative comparison only.
checkpoints.assumption: capture_fps_equivalent is model-dependent and usually undocumented; treat as unknown.

checkpoints.name: duplicate_frame_check
checkpoints.instruction: Check whether consecutive frame pairs are pixel-identical. Talbot's limit: 2 identical prints acceptable, 3 looks disjointed. Digital equivalence is our inference.

checkpoints.name: time_lapse_continuity_check
checkpoints.instruction: In playback: does change progress smoothly or in sudden steps? If steps appear, generative interval between keyframes may be too coarse.

explicit_gaps: AI generators do not expose capture_fps equivalent; CP2 ratio is partially undetermined.
Talbot's rates are for physical film; whether they predict AI temporal interpolation quality is untested.
Print-twice maps to frame duplication only by analogy; mechanism differs.
No audio, voice, likeness or face guidance; own invented subjects only.
combination_assumption: This contract treats the book's mechanism as a checklist frame, not a predictive model. It tells you what to look for, not what number to set.
